requirement: REL-1 — the physical two-machine demonstration; the viewer's broadcast freshness within 5 seconds
method: The browser's DOM carries a MutationObserver installed on the viewer's message list; it records the wall-clock instant each message card FIRST appears (a per-sequence set, so a catch-up page is recorded once and a live SSE frame is recorded at its arrival). The sender records the instant the server acknowledged its send (the api-client's own clock, immediately after the committed answer). The difference is the viewer's freshness.

same_clock_measurement.why: the sender and the viewer are the SAME machine (NSG-Mac-mini.local), so the difference carries NO clock-skew term at all
same_clock_measurement.sender: CLAUDE-MAC-1 (the Mac installation of the frozen portable package)
same_clock_measurement.verdict: pass — 0.107 s against the 5 s bound

cross_machine_measurement.why: the sender is the OTHER physical machine (ngs-staging), so the two clocks differ; the offset is measured, not assumed
cross_machine_measurement.sender: CLAUDE-STAGING-1 (the staging installation of the frozen Claude Code package)
cross_machine_measurement.clock_offset_method: the server's HTTP Date header is the common reference: 9 samples per client, the median of (client midpoint - server epoch). The header has 1-second resolution, so each median carries about +/-450 ms of quantization uncertainty.
cross_machine_measurement.reported_as: 0.00 s +/- 0.45 s (the raw difference is 0.102 s; the offset correction is within its own quantization)
cross_machine_measurement.verdict: pass — far inside the 5 s bound on any reading of the offset

honest_limits: The measurement is the DOM arrival of the message card, not the network arrival of the SSE frame; the SSE frame itself lands slightly earlier (the server polls the store every 250 ms and writes the frame immediately).
The cross-machine number carries the clock-offset uncertainty stated above; the same-clock number carries none.
Two canary measurements were taken per path; the earlier pair (seq 2 and seq 3) gave 120 ms and 113 ms raw — the same order of magnitude, so the result is not a single lucky sample.
